claims: The Artemis II SLS rocket is 322 feet tall.
The Saturn V is 363 feet tall.
The Artemis II SLS rocket offers ~15% more liftoff thrust than the Saturn V.
The SLS produces 8.8 million pounds of thrust at liftoff.
The Saturn V has 7.6 million pounds of thrust.
Saturn V used five F-1 engines (kerosene/oxygen) for the first stage.
SLS uses four RS-25 engines (hydrogen/oxygen) and two large solid rocket boosters.
Saturn V could deliver over 50 tons to Trans-Lunar Injection (TLI).
SLS Block 1 is designed for around 27 tons to Trans-Lunar Injection (TLI).
Artemis II features modern, fully digital avionics.
Artemis II features large flat-screen displays.
The 1960s/70s Apollo-era systems used analog systems and mechanical switches.
The Orion capsule carries four astronauts.
The Apollo Command Module carried three astronauts.
The Saturn V and SLS were both built to send human crews to the Moon and beyond.
The Saturn V and SLS both rely on multi-stage architecture to reach orbit.
The Saturn V and SLS both conclude with a splashdown in the ocean.
The Saturn V and SLS both have recovery by NASA teams.
SLS Block 1 is 98 meters (322 feet) tall.
Saturn V is 111 meters (363 feet) tall
